points.what: APAC contributed 46 orders to this week's growth, 143.8% of the total change, with APAC orders up 13.5% WoW.
points.so_what: APAC's gain outweighed declines elsewhere, meaning the week's order growth depended almost entirely on one region.

points.what: LATAM orders fell 30.4% WoW, subtracting 38 orders from the total change.
points.so_what: LATAM's pullback offset gains elsewhere and shows this week's order growth was uneven across regions.

points.what: Search contributed 34 orders to the week's growth, 106.2% of the total change, while Organic and Display both declined WoW.
points.so_what: Order growth this week came almost entirely from Search, with other traffic sources not adding to the gain.

points.what: AOV was $87.59, up 7.8% WoW but down 5.0% YoY.
points.so_what: Revenue growth this week came from bigger baskets, but baskets are still smaller than in the same week last year.

points.what: Cancellation rate was 16.4%, up 1.0 pp WoW and 1.3 pp YoY.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations represents $726 in revenue, so this week's increase reduces order quality even in a week that beat target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 2026-03-02 was 9.2%, down 1.4 pp WoW but up 2.2 pp YoY.
points.so_what: Even with the weekly improvement, returns remain higher than the same week last year, so the year-on-year rise has not reversed.

points.what: New signups fell to 214, down 9.3% WoW and 1.4% YoY.
points.so_what: Order growth this week did not come with matching growth in new customers, since signups are shrinking on both a weekly and yearly basis.

summary.headline: Orders and revenue beat target this week, but QTD and YTD revenue remain behind at 92.6%, with only one week left in the quarter.

points.what: Orders and revenue were 101.5% and 101.8% of target this week, both ahead.
points.so_what: The week met target, but that strength has not yet closed the quarter's earlier shortfall.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue are both 92.6% of target, with 1 week left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Despite this week beating target, both the quarter and year remain behind, and only one week remains in the quarter to close the gap.

points.what: Revenue rose 10.9% WoW, a notable jump, while AOV rose 7.8% WoW and orders rose 4.0% WoW.
points.so_what: Revenue growth this week came from higher order values, not more orders, since AOV grew faster than order count.

points.what: New signups fell 9.3% WoW and 1.4% YoY, a notable move outside the recent 8-week range.
points.so_what: Signups lagging behind order growth is a risk to sustaining order volume.

points.what: Weekly orders were 101.5% of target and weekly revenue was 101.8% of target this week.
points.so_what: The week itself met target on both orders and revenue.

points.what: QTD revenue is 92.6% of target with 1 week left in the quarter.
points.so_what: There is still $120,354 needed to reach the full-quarter target with only one week remaining, leaving little room to close the gap.

points.what: YTD revenue is 92.6% of target, with a required weekly run-rate of $78,893 to reach the full-year target.
points.so_what: The current 8-week run-rate of $56,578 is well below that required pace, keeping the full-year target out of reach at this rate.

points.what: Cancellation rate has risen for 3 straight weeks, from 14.3% to 16.4%.
points.so_what: A three-week rise in cancellations means the increase is not a one-off, adding risk to order quality heading into the new quarter.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate is $56,578, below the $78,893 needed weekly to hit the full-year target.
points.so_what: At the recent pace, the full-year revenue target is out of reach without a higher run-rate than the last 8 weeks.

points.what: New signups fell 9.3% WoW and 1.4% YoY, a notable move outside the recent 8-week range.
points.so_what: Continued signup declines are a risk to future order growth even though orders this week were ahead of target.
